Brush.description: Primary tool for drawing and painting on the canvas. Its properties (size, opacity, scatter, etc.) can be adjusted in the right-hand panel. Different brush types like Pen, Sketchy, and Pixel are available.

Eraser.description: Removes pixels from the active layer. It functions like a brush but makes pixels transparent.

Smudge Tool.description: Blends and pushes existing colors on the canvas without adding new color. [5]

Hand/Pan Tool.description: Moves the entire canvas view without altering the artwork. Useful for navigating a zoomed-in image. [1, 5]

Eyedropper.description: Selects a color from any pixel on the canvas and sets it as the current brush color. [1, 7]

Paint Bucket.description: Fills a contiguous area of similar color with the currently selected color. Settings like 'Tolerance' and 'Grow' can be adjusted. [1]

Gradient Tool.description: Creates a gradient fill by dragging a line on the canvas. The gradient transitions from the primary color to transparent by default. [5]

Shape Tool.description: Draws geometric shapes like rectangles, ellipses, and lines. [5]

Text Tool.description: Adds text to the canvas. Clicking on the canvas opens a dialog to type and format the text. [5]

Transform Tool.description: Allows for resizing, rotating, and moving the content of the active layer. [1]

Zoom.description: Zooms the canvas view in or out. Can be activated by holding Z and dragging horizontally, using the + and - keys, or using the mouse scroll wheel. [1]

brush_tool.description: Draws strokes on the canvas using the current color and brush settings.

pan_tool.description: Moves or pans the canvas view without drawing.

add_layer_button.description: Adds a new layer to the document.

redo_button.description: Re-applies the last action that was undone.

layer_visibility_toggle.description: Shows or hides the contents of the associated layer.

color_picker.description: Selects the active drawing color from a saturation/value field and a hue slider.

eyedropper_tool.description: Picks a color from the canvas and sets it as the active color.

brush_type_selector.description: Selects from a set of different brush rendering styles.

brush_size_control.description: Adjusts the size of the brush tip.

brush_opacity_control.description: Adjusts the opacity of the brush strokes.

brush_scatter_control.description: Adjusts the scatter effect of the brush strokes.

brush_shape_selector.description: Selects the shape of the brush tip from a set of presets.

lock_alpha_toggle.description: Toggles locking of the layer's alpha channel, preventing drawing on transparent pixels.

save_file_button.description: Saves or exports the current image.

share_button.description: Opens a dialog to share the image.

rules.rule: To draw a line: First, select a color from the color picker. Second, select the Brush tool ('B'). Third, adjust brush settings like Size ('[', ']') and Opacity. Finally, click and drag the mouse on the canvas.

To clear the entire canvas: Click the 'New' icon in the top right toolbar. In the subsequent dialog, confirm the desired canvas size and background color, then click 'OK'. Be aware this action is destructive and will replace the current image.

To save your work with layers: Click the 'Save' icon. From the dropdown menu, select 'Save PSD'. This will download a .psd file that preserves all layer information for future editing in Kleki or other compatible software. [1, 5]

To fill an area with color: First, select the desired color. Second, select the Paint Bucket tool. Third, adjust 'Tolerance' and 'Grow' settings as needed. Finally, click on the area of the canvas you wish to fill. For clean fills on line art, it is recommended to have the line art on a separate layer above the fill layer. [1]
To change a layer's opacity: Select the desired layer in the layers panel. Click on the 'Opacity' value (e.g., '100%') to reveal a slider. Drag the slider to the desired opacity level.

Kleki does not have a traditional auto-save feature to the cloud. It uses browser storage for recovery, which is device-specific. [5, 6] Use 'Ctrl+S' to save a PNG or 'Ctrl+Shift+S' to save to browser storage frequently to avoid losing work. [1, 3]
Saving as a PNG will flatten the image and discard all layer information. To preserve layers, you must save as a PSD file. [5]
Browser shortcuts (like Ctrl+W to close tab) can interfere with the application. Be mindful of which shortcuts are for the app versus the browser.

Some browsers have a 'memory saver' mode that can cause the tab to refresh when you switch away from it, potentially losing recent, unsaved changes. It's recommended to add kleki.com to the memory saver's exception list. [1]
Pressure sensitivity for styluses is supported but may require configuration in your browser or system settings to work correctly. [1]
Select a color from the color picker before drawing with the brush tool.
Adjust brush settings like size, opacity, and scatter before drawing to affect the stroke's appearance.
Select a target layer from the layers panel before drawing.
For architectural linework in Kleki, normalize render state first: brush tool, scatter 0, low stabilizer, very thin size, and full opacity before structural strokes.
Kleki documents Shift while drawing as a line tool; prefer this or a shape/line mode for straight architectural segments instead of unconstrained freehand brush strokes.

shortcuts.Ctrl+S: Save image as a PNG file. [1, 5]
shortcuts.Ctrl+Shift+S: Save image to browser's local storage. [1, 5]
shortcuts.Spacebar: Hold to temporarily activate Hand/Pan tool. [5]
shortcuts.Alt: Hold to temporarily activate Eyedropper tool. [7]
shortcuts.R: Hold and drag to rotate the canvas view. [1]
shortcuts.Z: Hold and drag horizontally to zoom. [1]
shortcuts.Enter: Fill the active layer with the current color. [5]
shortcuts.Ctrl+Alt: Show HUD Color Picker overlay near the cursor. [1]

modal_patterns.trigger: Clicking the 'New' icon (document with plus sign).
modal_patterns.handler: A dialog appears asking for canvas dimensions (width, height) and background color. Options include presets and a transparent background toggle. Click 'OK' to create the new canvas. This will replace the current work, so save first.

A dialog appears with options to save as 'PNG', 'PSD', or 'Layers (PNG)'. Selecting an option initiates a browser file download. No system 'Save As' dialog is shown directly; the file is typically saved to the browser's default 'Downloads' folder. [5, 9]
The standard operating system file picker dialog appears, allowing the user to select an image file to import onto a new layer. [10]

After clicking on the canvas with the Text Tool, a modal dialog appears. This dialog contains a text input field, and options for font, size, color, and formatting. The text updates on the canvas in real-time as you type. [5]

brush_opacity_slider.description: Adjusts the opacity of the current brush.

swap_colors_button.description: Swaps the primary and secondary colors.

brush_tool_button.description: Selects the brush tool for drawing architectural structure.

brush_stabilizer_control.description: Numeric stabilizer control for the current brush.

shape_tool_button.description: No stable on-screen anchor learned yet; prefer shortcut U for Kleki shape/line mode.

research_notes:
COLOR WORKFLOW: To change the active drawing color, use the color picker panel on the right. Click and drag within the large saturation/brightness square to pick a shade. Then, drag the slider below it to select the hue. Alternatively, click the '#' button to manually input a hex color code. The Eyedropper tool (shortcut: 'Alt') can also be used to pick a color directly from the canvas. Kleki uses a single-color system for its raster tools; there is no separate concept of 'stroke' and 'fill' colors like in vector applications. The selected color applies to the currently active tool (Brush, Paint Bucket, Shape, etc.).
